 “You lose focus and you see what happens like in the last game against Pakistan.” – Naushad Moosa
 India need just a point to seal top spot in the group, while the Maldives must win by three goals to progress. Naushad Moosa, however, is wary of their technical quality and wants his reshuffled side to maintain concentration until the final whistle. By Rahul Giri November 10, 2026 No Comments 3 Mins Read

 India sit on the brink of securing a spot in the SAFF Championship semi-finals as group leaders, needing just a single point in their final group-stage fixture against the Maldives.
 While the Blue Tigers hold a comfortable cushion, the Maldives face a monumental task: only a victory by a three-goal margin will take them into the knockout stages.
 The last meeting between the two sides came in March 2025, in a friendly that saw Sunil Chhetri temporarily step out of retirement to help India prepare for their Asian Cup Qualifier against Bangladesh in Shillong. India produced a dominant performance that evening, cruising to a 3-0 victory.
 Despite the Maldives suffering a 3-0 defeat to Pakistan in their tournament opener, India head coach Naushad Moosa is refusing to allow any room for complacency.
 “What I saw with Maldives is they are a very fast team, quick, they keep the ball well,” Moosa told RevSportz on the eve of the match. “Unfortunately, they conceded three goals. But otherwise, what I look at them is they are technically a very good team. And the way they move the ball, the build-up, everything, they are really good with it.”
 Moosa has had to reshape his squad at short notice following the departure of five players after the Pakistan fixture, bringing in seven fresh faces: Chinglensana Singh, Brison Fernandes, Irfan Yadwad, Macarton Nickson, Abdul Rabeeh, PV Vishnu and Sandip Mandi. However, the head coach views the adjustments as an opportunity rather than a setback, leveraging his prior experience with the incoming talent.
 “Instead of me worrying about the five players going and new players coming in, I should look for the solution. What better I can do to make this team combine well,” Moosa explained. “Most of the players who have come, they have played with me and they know the way we want to play. It’s been two years I am with the Under-23 team. You see Vishnu, Macarton \[Louis Nickson\] they all have played with me, so they know what kind of football I am looking for. That really helps us.”
 For the second consecutive match, India face an early 3:00 PM local kickoff. With temperatures hovering around 30°C under bright sunshine, the conditions present a tough physical challenge compared to the cooler evening slots.
 “I don’t think it makes much difference because the weather we have in India is the same,” Moosa said. “End of the day, players have to play, they have to run. Most of the players who are there have been playing regularly and they are fit.”
 The primary area of concern for the coaching staff remains defensive discipline in the closing stages. India conceded twice in stoppage time during their victory over Pakistan, a lapse Moosa wants eliminated before the knockouts begin. Additionally, tactical familiarity will be put to an immediate test, particularly in defence. With both Bijoy Varghese and Valpuia among the departing contingent, Moosa is forced to field a completely reshuffled backline.
 “It’s very important you stay consistent and, till the last whistle, stay focused,” Moosa emphasized. “You lose focus and you see what happens like in the last game against Pakistan. I will always tell my players to stay focused until the final whistle.”
